name: Ollama
description: Get up and running with large language models locally
longDescription: Ollama makes it easy to run open-source LLMs on your own hardware. Supports Llama 3, Mistral, Mixtral, and more.

configOptions.label: Models to pull on startup
configOptions.description: Comma-separated list of models to download

postDeployInstructions:
### Ollama First Steps

1. **Pull your first model:**
   ```bash
   docker exec -it ${PROJECT_NAME}-ollama ollama pull llama3.2
   ```

2. **Test the model:**
   ```bash
   docker exec -it ${PROJECT_NAME}-ollama ollama run llama3.2 "Hello!"
   ```

3. **Verify API is running:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags
   ```

**Recommended models:**
- `llama3.2` - Fast, general purpose (4.7GB)
- `mistral` - Great for coding (4.1GB)
- `llama3.2:1b` - Lightweight option (1.3GB)

📚 [Browse all models](https://ollama.ai/library)

name: Open WebUI
description: User-friendly WebUI for LLMs (formerly Ollama WebUI)
longDescription: Open WebUI is an extensible, feature-rich, and user-friendly self-hosted WebUI designed to operate entirely offline. It supports various LLM runners including Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs.

dependencies.description: Recommended LLM backend for local models

configOptions.label: Enable authentication
configOptions.description: Require login to access the UI

postDeployInstructions:
### Open WebUI Setup

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3000

2. **Create your admin account** (first user becomes admin)

3. **Configure Ollama connection:**
   - Go to Settings → Connections
   - Ollama URL should be: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Click "Verify Connection"

4. **Start chatting!** Select a model from the dropdown and begin.

**Tips:**
- Enable dark mode in Settings → Interface
- Import/export conversations via Settings
- Add custom system prompts per model

📚 [Open WebUI Documentation](https://docs.openwebui.com)

name: Qdrant
description: High-performance vector search engine with extended filtering support
longDescription: Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine with extended filtering support. It's designed for production-ready services with convenient API and out-of-the-box support for filtering.
postDeployInstructions:
### Qdrant Getting Started

1. **Verify the API is running:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:6333/readyz
   ```

2. **Access the Dashboard:** http://localhost:6333/dashboard

3. **Create your first collection:**
   ```bash
   curl -X PUT http://localhost:6333/collections/my_collection \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"vectors": {"size": 384, "distance": "Cosine"}}'
   ```

4. **List collections:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:6333/collections
   ```

**Integration URLs:**
- HTTP API: `http://qdrant:6333` (from Docker)
- gRPC API: `qdrant:6334`

📚 [Qdrant Documentation](https://qdrant.tech/documentation)

name: LangFlow
description: Visual framework for building multi-agent and RAG applications
longDescription: LangFlow is a low-code app builder for RAG and multi-agent AI applications. It's Python-based and agnostic to models and vector stores, with a visual IDE for drag-and-drop building.

configOptions.label: Database URL
configOptions.description: PostgreSQL connection string (optional, defaults to SQLite)

postDeployInstructions:
### LangFlow First Steps

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:7860

2. **Create a new flow:**
   - Click "New Project"
   - Drag components from the sidebar

3. **Connect to Ollama:**
   - Add an "Ollama" component
   - Set Base URL: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Select your model

4. **Build a simple RAG flow:**
   - Add: File Loader → Text Splitter → Embeddings → Vector Store → Chat
   - Connect the components
   - Click "Run"

**Tip:** Export flows as JSON for backup and sharing.

📚 [LangFlow Documentation](https://docs.langflow.org)

name: n8n
longDescription: n8n is a fair-code licensed workflow automation tool. It allows you to connect anything to everything via its open, fair-code model with 400+ integrations.

configOptions.label: Encryption key
configOptions.description: Key for encrypting credentials (auto-generated if empty)

postDeployInstructions:
### n8n Setup

1. **Open the editor:** http://localhost:5678

2. **Create your owner account** (first user becomes owner)

3. **Build your first workflow:**
   - Click "Add workflow"
   - Add a trigger (e.g., Manual, Schedule, Webhook)
   - Add action nodes
   - Click "Execute Workflow" to test

4. **Add AI capabilities:**
   - Search for "Ollama" in nodes
   - Configure with URL: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Use "Chat Model" or "Embeddings" nodes

**Popular integrations:** Slack, Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable

📚 [n8n Documentation](https://docs.n8n.io)

name: LocalAI
description: Drop-in replacement REST API compatible with OpenAI
longDescription: LocalAI is a drop-in replacement REST API that's compatible with OpenAI API specifications for local inferencing. It allows you to run LLMs, generate images, audio, and more locally or on-premises with consumer-grade hardware.

configOptions.label: Models to preload
configOptions.description: Comma-separated list of models to load on startup

postDeployInstructions:
### LocalAI Setup

1. **Verify API is running:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/readyz
   ```

2. **List available models:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/models
   ```

3. **Install a model from the gallery:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/models/apply \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"url": "github:mudler/LocalAI/gallery/llama3.yaml"}'
   ```

4. **Test with OpenAI-compatible call:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model": "llama3", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
   ```

**Note:** LocalAI is OpenAI API-compatible, so you can use any OpenAI SDK!

📚 [LocalAI Documentation](https://localai.io)

name: LM Studio
description: Desktop application for running LLMs locally with GUI
longDescription: LM Studio is a desktop application that makes it easy to run open-source LLMs locally on your machine. Note: LM Studio is primarily a desktop app, not a Docker service. It provides an OpenAI-compatible local server on port 1234.
externalServiceNote: LM Studio is a desktop application, not a Docker service. Install it from lmstudio.ai and start the local server to expose an OpenAI-compatible API on port 1234.
postDeployInstructions:
### LM Studio Setup (External Service)

⚠️ **LM Studio is a desktop application**, not a Docker service.

1. **Download LM Studio:** https://lmstudio.ai/

2. **Install and launch** the application

3. **Download a model:**
   - Go to the "Discover" tab
   - Search for a model (e.g., Llama 3)
   - Click "Download"

4. **Start the local server:**
   - Go to "Local Server" tab
   - Select your model
   - Click "Start Server"
   - Server runs on port 1234

5. **Connect from Docker services:**
   - Use URL: `http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1`
   - This allows Docker containers to reach your local LM Studio

📚 [LM Studio Docs](https://lmstudio.ai/docs)

name: vLLM
longDescription: vLLM is a fast and easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving. It features state-of-the-art serving throughput, efficient memory management with PagedAttention, and continuous batching.
postDeployInstructions:
### vLLM Setup (GPU Required)

⚠️ **Requires NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support**

1. **Verify GPU access:**
   ```bash
   docker exec -it ${PROJECT_NAME}-vllm nvidia-smi
   ```

2. **Check server status:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/health
   ```

3. **List loaded models:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/v1/models
   ```

4. **Test inference:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model": "meta-llama/Llama-3-8B", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 50}'
   ```

**Performance tips:**
- Use tensor parallelism for multi-GPU setups
- Enable KV cache quantization for memory savings

📚 [vLLM Documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai)

name: Text Generation WebUI
description: Gradio web UI for running LLMs like LLaMA, llama.cpp, and more
longDescription: A Gradio web UI for running Large Language Models like LLaMA, llama.cpp, GPT-J, Pythia, OPT, and GALACTICA. Its goal is to become the AUTOMATIC1111/stable-diffusion-webui of text generation.
postDeployInstructions:
### Text Generation WebUI Setup

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:7860

2. **Download a model:**
   - Go to "Model" tab → "Download model"
   - Enter a Hugging Face model name (e.g., `TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-GGUF`)
   - Click "Download"

3. **Load the model:**
   - Select the model from the dropdown
   - Choose the appropriate loader (llama.cpp for GGUF files)
   - Click "Load"

4. **Start chatting:**
   - Go to "Chat" tab
   - Select your character/persona
   - Begin conversation

**Tips:**
- Use GGUF format for efficient CPU/GPU inference
- Adjust context length in "Parameters" tab

📚 [Text Generation WebUI Wiki](https://github.com/oobabooga/text-generation-webui/wiki)

name: Chatbot UI
longDescription: Chatbot UI is an open-source AI chat app that allows users to create and deploy customizable AI chatbots. It's designed to be the best UI for interacting with AI models.
postDeployInstructions:
### Chatbot UI Setup

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3000

2. **Configure API key:**
   - Click the settings icon
   - Enter your OpenAI API key
   - Or configure a local endpoint

3. **Use with local models:**
   - Set `OPENAI_API_HOST` to your local API
   - For Ollama: `http://ollama:11434/v1`
   - For LocalAI: `http://localai:8080/v1`

4. **Start a conversation:**
   - Select a model
   - Type your message
   - Use `/` commands for quick actions

**Features:** Conversation folders, prompt templates, export/import

📚 [Chatbot UI GitHub](https://github.com/mckaywrigley/chatbot-ui)

name: LibreChat
description: Enhanced ChatGPT clone with multi-modal support
longDescription: LibreChat is a free, open-source AI chat platform that allows you to integrate multiple AI models in one interface. It supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, BingAI, ChatGPT, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic Claude, and more.
postDeployInstructions:
### LibreChat Setup

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3000

2. **Create your account** (registration required)

3. **Configure endpoints:**
   - Go to Settings → Endpoints
   - Add your API keys for providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

4. **Add local models:**
   - Configure Ollama endpoint: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Or LocalAI: `http://localai:8080`

5. **Start chatting:**
   - Select a provider from the dropdown
   - Choose a model
   - Begin your conversation

**Features:** Multi-provider, plugins, file uploads, conversation search

📚 [LibreChat Documentation](https://www.librechat.ai/docs)

name: Flowise
description: Drag & drop UI to build LLM flows with LangChain
longDescription: Flowise is an open-source low-code tool for developers to build customized LLM orchestration flows & AI agents. It's built on top of LangChain and provides a drag-and-drop interface.
postDeployInstructions:
### Flowise Setup

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3000

2. **Create your first chatflow:**
   - Click "Add New" → "Chatflow"
   - Drag components from the left sidebar

3. **Build a simple chat:**
   - Add: Chat Model (Ollama) → LLM Chain → Chat
   - Configure Ollama URL: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Connect the nodes
   - Click "Save" then "Chat"

4. **Add RAG capabilities:**
   - Add: Document Loader → Text Splitter → Embeddings → Vector Store
   - Connect to your vector database (Qdrant/Chroma)

**API Access:** Each chatflow gets a unique API endpoint for integration.

📚 [Flowise Documentation](https://docs.flowiseai.com)

name: Dify
description: LLM app development platform with RAG pipeline
longDescription: Dify is an open-source LLM app development platform. It combines Backend-as-a-Service and LLMOps, covering the core tech stack required for building generative AI-native applications.
postDeployInstructions:
### Dify Setup

⚠️ **Dify requires PostgreSQL and Redis** - make sure they're running.

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3000

2. **Create admin account:**
   - Complete the initialization wizard
   - Set your admin email and password

3. **Configure model providers:**
   - Go to Settings → Model Providers
   - Add OpenAI, Anthropic, or local models
   - For Ollama: Add as OpenAI-compatible with URL `http://ollama:11434/v1`

4. **Create your first app:**
   - Click "Create App"
   - Choose type: Chatbot, Text Generator, or Agent
   - Configure prompts and models
   - Publish and get API access

**Note:** Use docker-compose from [Dify repo](https://github.com/langgenius/dify) for full setup.

📚 [Dify Documentation](https://docs.dify.ai)

name: Chroma
description: Open-source embedding database for LLM applications
longDescription: Chroma is the open-source embedding database. It makes it easy to build LLM apps by making knowledge, facts, and skills pluggable for LLMs.
postDeployInstructions:
### Chroma Setup

1. **Verify API is running:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/heartbeat
   ```

2. **Create a collection:**
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/collections \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"name": "my_collection"}'
   ```

3. **List collections:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/collections
   ```

4. **Use with Python:**
   ```python
   import chromadb
   client = chromadb.HttpClient(host="localhost", port=8000)
   collection = client.get_or_create_collection("my_docs")
   ```

**Integration URL:** `http://chroma:8000` (from Docker containers)

📚 [Chroma Documentation](https://docs.trychroma.com)

name: Weaviate
longDescription: Weaviate is an open-source vector database that stores both objects and vectors, allowing for combining vector search with structured filtering. It's cloud-native and offers GraphQL and RESTful APIs.
postDeployInstructions:
### Weaviate Setup

1. **Check readiness:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/v1/.well-known/ready
   ```

2. **View schema:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/v1/schema
   ```

3. **Create a class:**
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/schema \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{
       "class": "Document",
       "vectorizer": "none",
       "properties": [{"name": "content", "dataType": ["text"]}]
     }'
   ```

4. **Use GraphQL playground:** http://localhost:8080/v1/graphql

**APIs available:**
- REST: `http://weaviate:8080`
- GraphQL: `http://weaviate:8080/v1/graphql`
- gRPC: `weaviate:50051`

📚 [Weaviate Documentation](https://weaviate.io/developers/weaviate)

name: Milvus
description: Highly scalable vector database for massive embeddings
longDescription: Milvus is an open-source vector database built to power embedding similarity search and AI applications. It makes unstructured data search more accessible and provides a consistent user experience.
postDeployInstructions:
### Milvus Setup

⚠️ **Milvus requires etcd and MinIO** - use the official docker-compose.

1. **Check health:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:9091/healthz
   ```

2. **Use with Python (pymilvus):**
   ```python
   from pymilvus import connections, Collection
   connections.connect(host="localhost", port="19530")
   ```

3. **Create a collection:**
   ```python
   from pymilvus import CollectionSchema, FieldSchema, DataType
   fields = [
       FieldSchema(name="id", dtype=DataType.INT64, is_primary=True),
       FieldSchema(name="embedding", dtype=DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=384)
   ]
   schema = CollectionSchema(fields)
   collection = Collection("my_collection", schema)
   ```

**Recommended:** Use [Attu](https://github.com/zilliztech/attu) for GUI management.

📚 [Milvus Documentation](https://milvus.io/docs)

name: AnythingLLM
description: All-in-one AI application with built-in RAG and document processing
longDescription: AnythingLLM is a full-stack application that transforms any document, resource, or content into a contextualized chatbot. It includes built-in vector database, RAG pipeline, and multi-user support.

configOptions.label: Ollama URL
configOptions.description: URL for Ollama API (if using Ollama)

postDeployInstructions:
### AnythingLLM Getting Started

1. **Open the interface:** http://localhost:3001

2. **Complete initial setup:**
   - Choose your LLM provider (Ollama recommended for local)
   - Set Ollama URL: `http://ollama:11434`
   - Select your embedding model

3. **Create your first workspace:**
   - Click "New Workspace"
   - Give it a name
   - Upload documents (PDF, TXT, DOCX, etc.)

4. **Start chatting with your documents!**
   - Ask questions about your uploaded content
   - AnythingLLM automatically creates embeddings

**Key features:**
- Built-in vector database (no external DB needed)
- Multi-user support with permissions
- API access for integrations

📚 [AnythingLLM Documentation](https://docs.anythingllm.com)
